label: copy-phase input "1" (fed-back digit 1) from the 3rd recalled position on
explanation: Fires almost exclusively when the input during the copy phase is the digit 1 (i.e. the model just output 1 and it is fed back). 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase and on in_tok==1; it never fires in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on other tokens (a few dozen tiny activations on other tokens). It is almost silent when the 1 is at recall_idx 1, weak and unreliable at recall_idx 2 (~1.3% rate, small magnitude, most false positives there), and reliable from recall_idx >= 3. Firing rate rises with the number of digits in the sequence. The strongest activations occur on the first of a pair of consecutive 1s (e.g. ...1 1 ...); the second 1 activates more weakly. Lowest-quartile examples are 1s fed back early in the copy phase. Predicate (in_tok==1 in copy phase, recall_idx>=3): dev P 0.98, R 0.90, F1 0.94, mass recall 0.97; dropping the recall_idx condition to >=2 gives R 0.999 with P 0.85.

issues: The core finding holds. All activation mass is in the copy phase (original phase 0, delimiter 0) and 1.000 of the mass is on in_tok==1. Recall_idx 1 has only 3 activations. Test scores reproduce: P 0.983, R 0.896, F1 0.937, mass recall 0.971.

The '~1.3% rate at recall_idx 2' claim is misleading. 1.3% is the rate over ALL recall_idx==2 steps. When the fed-back token actually is 1, the feature fires on 38% of those steps (P=0.384 for (phase==2)&(in_tok==1)&(recall_idx==2)). Those firings carry only 2.8% of the mass, and they are mostly small: 37% coverage of the bottom activation quartile.

Firing at recall_idx==2 depends systematically on length, which the explanation calls 'unreliable'. With in_tok==1 at recall_idx 2, the firing rate is 0.74 at L=3, 0.82 at L=4 and 0.48 at L=5, then 0.21-0.30 at L>=6. So a fed-back 1 that was the 2nd original token fires reliably in short sequences.
The claim that the firing rate rises with n_digits is a base-rate artifact: more digits means more 1s. Within the predicate, precision is flat (0.978 at n_digits==1, 0.986 at n_digits>=3).

Small point on the label: 'from the 3rd recalled position on' means recall_idx>=3, i.e. the fed-back 1 was original token index >=2. That is correct but easy to misread. Precision at recall_idx==3 is slightly lower (0.94; 0.92 at L=6). The test-split false positives (1005) are mostly 1s at original index 2 in longer sequences, so they are a soft boundary rather than noise.
The consecutive-1s claim is only anecdotal, from the top examples. It covers a tiny slice: prev_tok==1 within the predicate is about 3% of recall.
